title: Reaching St. Louis and being collected by Bennie Moten
summary: They hoboed on to St. Louis, slept in 20-cent beds, and Moten sent cars for Smith, Lester Young and Ross, which put them in his band.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So we stayed there a day, and then we come on down to St. Louis, and when we got to St. Louis, Bennie Moten heard that we were...
Did you hobo again to St. Louis?
Yes.
What was that like? Just as bad?

No. That was all right. It wasn't long that we was in St. Louis. We hoboed mostly in the daytime, and went on down there. We got there late one evening in the next couple of days after we left Cincinnati. We went down there, and we still had that change left. I had two dollars and forty cents left, and we went on down there and got one of them 20-cent beds. 20
Buster Smith - 215
cents. Sleep all night. There was nothin' in there but a bunch of men and them little old cots in a building.
Ross and I stayed there a couple of days. Then Bennie heard about us being over there, and he sent three cars over there and picked us up.
You must have been glad to hear from him.
Yeah, sure did. And that's the way we got in his band. Lester Young, all three of us.
Why did Eddie Barefield leave the band? Because Eddie must have left before you...
Oh yeah, yeah. Eddie left a long time before that.
Oh, really?
Yeah. He was in the band...
In '32 or something...
Yeah... In '32?
You must have joined in '33.
Yeah, maybe so.
Those records were made in '32.
We left, and went on with Cab Calloway or somebody.
What would have happened to you if you'd got caught hoboeing on the train?
They didn't bother you.
Buster Smith - 216
So the police caught you...

Yeah, they caught us. But they didn't bother us, as long as we didn't go in none of them cars that had merchandise in them. Because Ross got to running down through there, and then they told us..> Two of them detectives were (?). They said, "Man, don't run. They'll shoot you." And he run, and he come on up there and he told us what had happened, and they said, "Well, don't be hanging around them cars with that food and stuff in there." We said, "We just tryin' to get home, tryin' to get home..." And they left us alone.
